THE PICK CRITERION WHEN THE SHEET LANDS: British, not generic European.
Canon wants a wet northern port town's rectangular dressed granite block,
blue-grey to black, not the small rounded warm-toned stone the Prague
description implies. Overrule rank order BY LOOKING, the same way the kerb
pick was overruled by the Hook sheet's own QUAY STONE swatch rather than
taken by name.
READ OFF THE HOOK SHEET ITSELF, 2026-09-21, not off its swatch strip. The
street panel's ground was cropped at 2x and looked at as one rectangle
(production/art/atlas-01/concepts/hook.png on origin/art/atlas-01, the
approved reference under D41). What it shows, and it sharpens this brief:
- THE BLOCKS ARE RECTANGULAR AND LAID IN REGULAR COURSES, running across
the street rather than in a fan or a radial pattern. Anything fanned,
radial or randomly coursed is wrong for Meridian however good it looks,
and ambientCG's PavingStones set carries a lot of both.
- THE TONE IS COOL AND NARROW. Grey to grey-brown dry, near-black wet,
with the joints barely readable under water. A warm or a high-chroma
candidate is wrong before its pattern is even judged.
- ROAD AND PAVEMENT ARE BOTH BLOCK-LAID AND THEY DIFFER BY SCALE AND
WEAR, not by family. The carriageway is darker, flatter and more worn;
the pavement beside Mickey's is a crisper block in tighter courses.
THAT LAST POINT CORRECTS THE SECOND CRITERION RATHER THAN DROPPING IT. The
criterion was 'the pick must not read as sidewalk', since sidewalk.jpg IS
PavingStones067 out of this same category. The reference says a blanket
must-not-resemble is too strong: in a British port street the pavement and
the carriageway ARE the same family of stone. What the pick must not be is
INDISTINGUISHABLE from sidewalk.jpg at the same scale, which is a comparison
and not an impression, so it is made in one picture at one scale against the
shipped file rather than from two looks minutes apart (instruments.md).
